spec: Poison: at End of Phase deal damage equal to its value to the holder, then reduce the value by 1. Stacking additive. Source: the zombie's Rotting Bite applies poison 2 on hit.
expect: a unit with poison 3 takes 3 then 2 then 1 and the status is gone on turn 4

spec: Burn: same tick as poison, and halves all healing received while held. Source: a new terrain status is out of scope here — give the Mage's staff bolt a burn 2 rider. Declares changesBaseline.
expect: burn 3 deals 3/2/1; healing while burning is halved, rounded down

spec: Add forest, rocky, rocky-hills, water, obstacle to TERRAIN alongside OPEN and HILLS, and teach terrainOf() their glyphs (f r R w x) from MAP-01's legend. NO RULES YET — every new kind behaves exactly like open. This item is pure plumbing and must be provably behaviour-neutral.
expect: map.field loads its real 7-terrain layout instead of collapsing to open/hills, and all four original baselines are BYTE-IDENTICAL because no existing map contains a new glyph
note: If a baseline moves, the plumbing leaked into behaviour. That is the whole point of doing this as its own item.

spec: moveCostOf gains a case per kind. SWITCH, do not decide: forest 2, rocky 2, rocky-hills 2, water 3-or-impassable, obstacle impassable. map.json leaves moveCost null ON PURPOSE — these are design decisions. Put each in SWITCHES.md with a default and let a sweep answer.
expect: reachable() shrinks on map.field relative to terrain.kinds, and the shrink is larger for a move-4 unit than a move-5 unit

spec: An impassable hex cannot be entered: reachable() never returns it and pathTo() never routes through it. Obstacles are impassable. Water passability is a SWITCH. This is the first terrain that can make a hex unreachable, so it is also the first that can strand a unit.
expect: no path on map.field ever enters an obstacle hex across 200 battles, and no battle ends capped because a unit could not find a route

spec: Terrain grants stat modifiers through the EXISTING stat pipeline — rows in terrainMods(), not new stations. Forest +10 dodge +1 armor. Water -10 accuracy. Rocky-hills as hills. Values are SWITCHES; map.json leaves coverBonus and modifiers null on purpose.
expect: a unit standing in forest shows terrain.forest rows in its effective(dodge) ledger, and hit rate against it drops measurably in a paired sweep
note: This should be almost free. The stat pipeline landed for exactly this — if it needs a pipeline change, something is wrong with the design, not the item.

spec: A standing unit exerts ZoC on its six adjacent hexes. A unit that ENTERS a hex inside an enemy ZoC stops there — it may enter, then its movement ends. Downed and dead units exert nothing. THE AI IS DELIBERATELY BLIND TO THIS (Angela, 2026-08-13): it keeps its current scoring, picks a destination as if ZoC did not exist, and gets stopped short. That is accepted, not a defect.
expect: a unit pathing past an adjacent zombie ends its move on the first hex inside that zombie's ZoC, and the log carries move.stopped naming the unit that stopped it
note: BECAUSE THE AI IS BLIND: reachable() still offers hexes the unit cannot actually reach, so units will routinely end up somewhere they did not choose. That MUST emit move.stopped. A unit ending somewhere unexplained with no log line is the exact silent-failure class the harness exists to catch.

spec: Leaving a hex inside an enemy's ZoC provokes one free attack from that enemy, resolved through performAttack with its cheapest melee attack, then settle. Once per enemy per activation. Costs the attacker nothing. AI remains blind — it will walk into these.
expect: a kiting ranger adjacent to a zombie takes a hit when it disengages, the log shows the attack with causeId movement.aoo, and the ranger's damage-taken share rises measurably in a paired sweep
note: HAZARD: this lands damage MID-MOVE, so settle can fire inside executeMove's per-step loop. A unit can die between two steps, and victory can trigger mid-activation. executeMove already breaks on lifeState !== standing; that guard is now load-bearing and needs its own test.

spec: Regeneration: at End of Phase heal its value, then reduce by 1. Never above max HP. Source: a new Warrior class power 'Second Wind', 1 stamina, cooldown 4, grants regen 3 to self.
expect: regen 3 on a damaged unit heals 3 then 2 then 1, capped at max HP

spec: Weakness: lowers damage DEALT by 1 per point (not the Strength/Precision stats), reduces by 1 at End of Phase. Source: a new Ghoul enemy attack 'Sapping Claw' applying weakness 2. Add the Ghoul as part of this item.
expect: a warrior with weakness 2 does axe damage minus 2; the stat itself is unchanged

spec: Stunned: the unit cannot act at all, reduces by 1 at End of Phase. Source: the Ghoul Brute's heavy attack applies stun 1 on hit.
expect: a stunned unit produces no move and no primary, and the log says why

spec: Protection: reduces incoming damage at station 550 AND is reduced by the damage it absorbs. Also loses 1 at End of Phase. Additive when granted again. Source: landed together with ability.warrior.rally, which grants it.
expect: protection 3 hit for 2 absorbs 2 and drops to 1; then End of Phase takes it to 0

spec: Skeleton Archer: enemy, ranged role, 6 HP, 0 armour, 0 resist, 70 accuracy, 2 strength, 3 precision, movement 3, shortbow reach 4 precision physical.
expect: appears, kites, shoots, dies; zombies still behave unchanged

spec: Ghoul Brute: enemy, melee role, 18 HP, 2 armour, 55 accuracy, 6 strength, movement 3, one heavy attack at Strength +2.
expect: a slow heavy enemy that survives multiple hero turns

spec: Rally: warrior class power, grants Protection 2 to every ally within 2 hexes, 1 stamina, cooldown 4. Requires status.protection.
expect: every ally inside the radius gains protection 2; nobody outside does

spec: Volley: ranger class power, two separate bow hits against the same target, each rolling to hit independently. 2 stamina, cooldown 3.
expect: two to-hit rolls and up to two damage events per use; armour applies per hit

spec: Defender mode: stays within 2 hexes of the nearest ally with less than half HP, attacks anything adjacent, never advances alone.
expect: a defender never ends further than 2 from its charge while that ally lives

spec: Support mode: holds at range, prefers using abilities on allies over attacking, retreats when threatened.
expect: exercises the support role, which is currently declared and unused

spec: NOT A DEFECT — Angela: the Mage/Ranger split is intentional. The Mage deals MAGIC damage and the Ranger PHYSICAL, which diverge sharply once enemies carry armor; and the Mage has Arcane Bolt and more to come, while the Ranger is essentially just its attack. Raw damage-per-swing is therefore the wrong yardstick. What is still worth measuring: the staff is only distinguishable from the bow against a target with armor > 0, and every enemy in the game today has armor 0. Add an armored enemy, then sweep staff vs bow against it.
expect: against an armored enemy the Mage out-damages the Ranger, and against an unarmored one it does not — the split is visible in the sweep, not just in the design
note: Open question that IS real: attack.mage.strike was used 0 times in 300 battles, the same dead-content shape as Massive Strike. The melee option on a ranged unit may never be worth taking.
